utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Let me start from apologising to Mr. Brdjanin, particularly, and to Mr. Ackerman, and to the representatives of the Prosecution for a slight delay this morning which was for inevitable reasons. We will now start with our proceedings. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-99-36-A, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances of the parties. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Steffen Wirth appearing for the Office of the Prosecutor. With me my colleague Katharina Margetts, and our case manager is Ms. Lourdes Galicia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wirth. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I'm John Ackerman. I'm here for Mr. Brdjanin. And I hope you recover quickly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Brdjanin, I want to make sure that you can follow the proceedings in a language you understand. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] First of all, good morning to everyone. Yes, I can understand and follow the proceedings in the language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brdjanin. You may be seated. This is, as you know, a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation to -- including the mental and physical condition of that person. The last Status Conference in this case was held on 18 October 2006. Almost 120 days have now passed since that Status Conference. I note that on the 7th December and the 8th December, 2006, we had the appeal hearings in this case. I want you all, and particularly Mr. Brdjanin, to know that we continue to work hard on reviewing the appeals and on preparing the judgement which we will be issued in due course. Mr. Brdjanin, do you have any issues that you would like to raise at this time, particularly any concerns regarding your mental and physical well-being? Mr. Brdjanin? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] No, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brdjanin. Before concluding the Status Conference, I want to ask counsel for the Prosecution and Defence whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this point. Mr. Wirth?

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Nothing from our side, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We have nothing, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. As there are no other issues, I thank the parties for their attendance and call the proceedings to a close.
